topic: Transactional outbox: saving to the database and publishing an event can't be atomic, so write the event to an outbox table in the same transaction
text:
Your order is saved, but the "order created" event never went out. Now billing doesn't know the order exists.

That's the dual-write problem: one operation writes to the database and to a message broker, and there's no guarantee both succeed.

• Publish before commit: the transaction can still roll back, and downstream acts on an order that doesn't exist.
• Publish after commit: the service can crash in between, and the event is lost.

The fix (transactional outbox): insert the event into an outbox table in the same transaction as the business data. A separate relay reads that table and publishes to the broker. Messages go out if, and only if, the transaction commits.

The catch: the relay can publish a message more than once, for example if it crashes after publishing but before marking it sent. So consumers have to be idempotent.

My rule of thumb: if an event matters to money or inventory, use an outbox. For a harmless notification, a plain publish after commit is often enough.

How does your team keep database writes and events in sync?

image.alt: Diagram: an order row and an outbox event row are inserted in one database transaction, then a relay publishes the event to a message broker. Signed Ali Hassan, alihexan.com
